hiiaka-local-view-preparation.prompt: Create a new independent research-guided hypothetical observer illustration, 1672 x 941 pixels, a wide local view from Hiʻiaka, the unresolved moon of Haumea. Use independently invented neutral grey granular regolith, scattered angular blocks, modest shallow depressions and low ridges, a low distant horizon and a black sky. Quiet scientific visualization, restrained sunlight and plausible shadows, but no claim of measured materials, terrain, colour, illumination or registered site. Do not reproduce or recolour any observed body's map, image or terrain. Do not use Namaka, Haumea, the Moon, Pluto or another body's geography. No astronomical disks, Sun, planets, moons, rings or stars in this camera frame; this is an assumed camera direction, not a claim they are invisible. No atmosphere, haze, clouds, active plume, exposed liquid or ocean, biology, vehicles, people or survivable landing implication. Hiʻiaka's rapid nonsynchronous rotation does not establish a permanently Haumea-facing site. Shape, pole and observer normal are not independently registered. Place two clear readable footer lines on a discreet dark strip: 'IMAGINED — LOCAL VIEW FROM HIʻIAKA' and 'Terrain, materials, colour and lighting are hypothetical'. Preserve the distinction between an artistic scene and measured science. Render a finished independent illustration, not a collage.

geometry.limits: Angular outputs only; colour and irradiance discarded. Each projected semiaxis is passed separately as a spherical scale surrogate, not an exact finite-distance triaxial limb calculation. The 1006±67/572±15km projected axes belong to the 2025-03-16 Earth view, not the directions from either moon. These examples MUST NOT be adopted as actual moon-view axes, a simultaneous ellipse, a registered Haumea disk, or a confidence envelope.

scienceLimits: Haumea is a rotating triaxial body. A full moon-view limb requires physical principal axes, rotation phase, body pole, observer direction and surface-normal registration. The gravity reference radius772km is not substituted for those physical axes. Existing smooth ellipsoid and all native/model bytes remain unchanged.

Nominal semimajor axes at JD2454615.0 are scales, not current distances. Namaka eccentricity.220 and Hiʻiaka.0604 preclude treating these as dated separations. No orbital uncertainty propagation or current ephemeris is claimed.

Subtracting an assumed spherical moon height is illustrative only; neither size assumption establishes local normal, spin synchronization, permanent Haumea-facing terrain or everywhere-visible primary.

Haumea model interior densities, ring surface density analogies and fossil rotation are not moon chemistry, texture, spin or observed history. No analog skin, atmosphere, plume, ocean, biology or landing scene adopted.
The 2026 primary record CC BY-NC-SA4.0 is distinct from NASA image/raw-data terms. No figure used. Native 2015 point identity/product/filter/UTC crossmatch remains open.
